description: How an NPC meets the party: starting attitude by role (standard 2024 Friendly / Indifferent / Hostile scale), speech style, temperament toward flattery, flirting, threats, lies and bribes (colour only, never a mechanical benefit; every line is family-suitable warmth, wit or banter), a deflection for 'what are you hiding', and the frames that assemble prepared answers from lines the NPC may say freely. tag_vocabulary, incompatible and trait_tags implement the agreement rule: a chosen style or reaction never clashes with the mannerism, speech direction or voice the chapter generator already gave the NPC. Original prose.

entries.vocabulary: plain, small words; says only what is meant
entries.tic: ends a point with a flat 'That's the lot.'

entries.vocabulary: homely and affectionate; calls people 'friend'
entries.tic: circles back to the start of a thought

entries.vocabulary: exact and formal; never contracts a word
entries.tic: begins corrections with 'To be exact.'

entries.vocabulary: understatement and dry asides
entries.tic: adds a one-word verdict such as 'Naturally.'

entries.vocabulary: words in a rush; half-finished sentences
entries.tic: apologises mid-sentence

entries.vocabulary: blunt and low; swallows the ends of words
entries.tic: grunts before answering

entries.vocabulary: tells every answer as a little tale with a sting at the end
entries.tic: ends with 'And that's how it was.'

entries.vocabulary: answers questions with questions
entries.tic: meets a question with 'Now why do you ask?'

entries.vocabulary: bright and lilting, with a rhythm like a rhyme
entries.tic: lets every line rise at the end; closes with 'So it goes.'

entries.vocabulary: weighs every word; leaves long pauses
entries.tic: says 'Let me think' before every answer

entries.vocabulary: sincere to the point of awkwardness
entries.tic: says 'I mean that.'

entries.vocabulary: old sayings and weather-wisdom
entries.tic: ends with 'Mark that.'

entries.vocabulary: orders and reports; no wasted breath
entries.tic: closes every point with 'That's an end of it.'

entries.vocabulary: half-hints; lowers the voice; glances about
entries.tic: says 'Keep it to yourself.'

entries.vocabulary: loud and jolly; laughs mid-sentence
entries.tic: laughs before the end of the line

entries.vocabulary: soft and tired; trails off at the end
entries.tic: sighs a soft 'Ah.' first

entries.vocabulary: boasts and teases; gives everyone a nickname
entries.tic: calls the listener 'chief'

entries.vocabulary: polite words with no warmth under them
entries.tic: opens with 'How kind.' whatever was said

entries.vocabulary: quick and squeaky; repeats words for emphasis
entries.tic: doubles every second word

entries.vocabulary: mumbles; apologises as they go
entries.tic: begins with 'Um.'

entries.text: warms to it and shows it
entries.speak: Well, that is kind of you to say. I will try not to let it go to my head.

entries.text: suspects it and asks what is really wanted
entries.speak: Praise is cheap. What do you want?

entries.text: waves it away, embarrassed but secretly pleased
entries.speak: Oh, stop. Really. Go on, though.

entries.text: laughs and returns the compliment with interest
entries.speak: Flattery from you? I will take it, and I will give you double.

entries.text: accepts it as no more than their due
entries.speak: You are not wrong. But it is pleasant to hear.

entries.text: is touched, then becomes a little guarded
entries.speak: That is more than I expected. Thank you.

entries.text: turns it toward the work, never toward themselves
entries.speak: It is the work that deserves the praise, not me.

entries.text: melts and begins to talk too much
entries.speak: Oh, you do go on! I could listen to you all evening.

entries.text: flattered but spoken for, and says so with a smile
entries.speak: I am flattered, truly. But my heart is already spoken for, so save your charms for someone who can use them.

entries.text: amused and teasing; gives as good as gets
entries.speak: Bold! Keep that up and I might ask you to carry my bags.

entries.text: flustered; loses the thread of the sentence
entries.speak: Oh, well, what was I saying? You have scattered my thoughts.

entries.text: cool and unimpressed; the compliment slides off
entries.speak: Save the charm. It will not buy you anything here.

entries.text: plays along only to learn something
entries.speak: Is that so? Do go on. I am always curious how far a smile will get someone.

entries.text: gently and kindly declines
entries.speak: That is a kind thing to say, and I will remember it. But no.

entries.text: politely returns to the matter at hand
entries.speak: How kind. Now, about the matter at hand.

entries.text: is baffled, then blushes and goes quiet
entries.speak: Thank you, I think. Is it warm in here?

entries.text: stands firm, voice steady
entries.speak: Threaten me all you like. I have lived through worse than words.

entries.text: bristles and threatens back, loudly
entries.speak: You will want to watch your tone. I know more people in this town than you would guess.

entries.text: goes pale and begins to talk fast
entries.speak: Please. There is no need for that. Tell me what you want to know and I will tell you.

entries.text: answers with quiet, cold courtesy
entries.speak: I would advise against that. I would advise it very politely.

entries.text: laughs it off to hide the fear
entries.speak: Ha! Very good. Do it again, with more feeling.

entries.text: glances at the door and lowers the voice
entries.speak: I would keep your voice down. The walls here have ears, and the ears have friends.

entries.text: folds quickly and gives up something small, but nothing important
entries.speak: Fine. Fine! Take this much, and not a word more.

entries.text: refuses flatly and goes silent
entries.speak: No. Nothing more to say.

entries.text: believes it too easily
entries.speak: Is that right? Well, if you say so.

entries.text: notices at once and says so kindly
entries.speak: That does not sit right, friend. But I will let it pass.

entries.text: pretends to believe it and watches closely
entries.speak: Mm. Of course. Please, go on.

entries.text: catches it and calls it out bluntly
entries.speak: That is not true, and we both know it. Try again.

entries.text: becomes confused and asks too many questions
entries.speak: But that does not fit. Wait, who said that, and when?

entries.text: is hurt by it more than angry
entries.speak: I would rather you simply told me. It hurts a little, you know.

entries.text: plays along, then turns the lie around with a joke
entries.speak: Oh, wonderful. Tell me another. I do enjoy a good one.

entries.text: weighs it against what they know and says nothing
entries.speak: Hm. I will think on that.

entries.text: refuses, offended
entries.speak: Put that away. I am not for sale, and I do not care for the notion.

entries.text: refuses with dignity, though tempted
entries.speak: I thank you, but no. My good name is the only thing I own outright.

entries.text: takes it at once and promises nothing
entries.speak: Thank you. I will note your generosity. I will note nothing else.

entries.text: haggles for more
entries.speak: Is that all? You can do better than that.

entries.text: is embarrassed and pushes it back
entries.speak: Oh, no. No, I could not. Please, take it back.

entries.text: accepts, then offers a harmless scrap of gossip in return
entries.speak: Well, since you are so generous: the baker's cat has had kittens again.

entries.text: asks what it is meant to buy before deciding
entries.speak: What exactly is this meant to buy?

entries.text: tells them to give it to someone who needs it more
entries.speak: Give it to someone who needs it. I am not short.

entries.text: jokes about a harmless embarrassment
entries.speak: Hiding? A very bad singing voice, and you will never hear it.

entries.text: turns it into a gentle confession of something trivial
entries.speak: Everyone hides something. Mine is a sore back, and I would be grateful if you did not tell.

entries.text: pretends not to have heard
entries.speak: That is a strange question. I will pretend I did not hear it.

entries.text: dismisses the question curtly
entries.speak: Nothing worth your time.

entries.text: turns the question around
entries.speak: I could ask you the same.

entries.text: stands on privacy
entries.speak: My private business is mine. I am sure yours is yours.

entries.text: teases back
entries.speak: If I were hiding something I would hardly say so. Would you?

entries.text: stammers and over-denies
entries.speak: No. No, there is nothing. Why would you think that?

entries.text: puts it off gently
entries.speak: Ask me again when we know each other better.

entries.text: jokes about hiding from their own cooking
entries.speak: I am hiding from my own cooking, mostly.

entries.text: stays calm and gives nothing
entries.speak: Whatever you imagine, you are probably wrong.

entries.text: says nothing at all and asks for the next question
entries.speak: Next question, please.
